text:
Sam Malinski went undrafted out of Cornell and became, by Evolving-Hockey's measure, the eighth most valuable defenseman in the league last season, 3.1 wins above replacement, mostly from defense. This season the Avalanche are leaning on him more, especially with Nathan MacKinnon out.

He still doesn't have a goal: zero on 38 shots and 1.8 expected, a small and fixable drought for a defenseman. The more interesting number is the luck around him. Colorado has scored 13.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, a huge figure that will fade, and yet his own points (nine in 22) sit below his talent range. The play underneath is solid: 54% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) puts his primary shot assists at the 95th percentile among defensemen, so he's creating more than his assists show. Our range projects 31 to 49 points.
